newsitem.title: USA: Pope & Talbot reports higher Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: Pope & Talbot reports higher Q2 results.

text.p: Pope & Talbot Inc Tuesday reported second quarter profits of $3.98 million or $0.30 a share, up sharply from the year-ago quarter's results of $662,000, or $.05 a share.
Revenues of $124,837,000 for the second quarter increased 13 percent over the second quarter of 1996 and 7 percent over last quarter.

The company said operating results from the company's lumber mills were higher than prior periods. Lumber prices continued to be strong and shipment volume increased at all five facilities over the last quarter as production remained high and inventory levels were reduced.
Pulp losses continued in the second quarter, but results were improved over last quarter. Pulp prices were improved while fiber prices were lower at the Halsey pulp mill.
The company said its tissue business continued to make steady improvements in the second quarter.

Operating profits were dramatically higher than a year ago and 34 percent higher than last quarter as higher sales volumes and lower production costs more than offset the impact of lower sales prices.

"As the Company's performance deteriorated in 1995, we took action by disposing of under performing assets and renewed our focus on manufacturing efficiencies, particularly in our tissue business," Peter Pope, chairman and chief executive officer, said. "Today, with the help of strong lumber markets, we are seeing the benefits of our hard work.

"The company's annualized return on equity was 9 percent for the quarter, a significant improvement over 3 percent last quarter and 1 percent for the same period a year ago," he said. "While we still have much work to do, I am encouraged by our improved performance."
